      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "3d7eb02b64085d2082b7963997a4ce98a7c6aa2c": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-27T16:24:07Z",
      "body": "The maintainer accepts ADR 0006 on 2026-09-27. The Omnigent M0 pilot is\ndropped; the adoption path starts at M1; parallel sessions run from then\non, every writing session beyond the first in a worktree of its own, at\nmost writing_sessions_per_repository of them (lakeswitch-ai D-59, D-60).\nThe first writing session writes the tracker; a worker session claims its\nown bead and adds its handover comment, nothing more, as D-60 has it. The\nworker claim waits until the maintainer rewrites AGENTS.md house rule 4.\nThe D-60 write guard takes the place of ADR 0005's Omnigent session\npolicy; it does not exist yet, so until it does, the bounds are stated,\nnot enforced.\n\nADR 0001 is superseded; ADR 0002 and ADR 0005 are superseded in part.\nEach records it in its header. The target document carries a notice at\nits top, in the D-3 and D-7 rows and in its tracker section; its other M0\npassages stay as the record of the earlier design.\n\nOwed item Coding Harness 3 of the lakeswitch-ai decision record.\n\nPrepared by a Claude Code session (the ADR, these notes, this message);\nthe maintainer asked for the acceptance to be prepared as a draft, and an\nagent review in a fresh context read it before signing. The explain-back\nand this commit are the maintainer's, signed with the Touch-ID key.\n\nExplain-back:\nhe owed decision record lands as one signed bundle per repository — coding-harness and lakeswitch-ai — putting the ratified decisions into the files they name.\nhe decisions are ratified and in force; only their promotion is owed, and bundling keeps it reviewable as single signed acts under gate M-30.\nThe bundle edits the very files the guard and gates read, so a wrong entry hits the enforcement layer itself — hence one Bead per item,\n\nPrepared-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "3d7eb02b64085d2082b7963997a4ce98a7c6aa2c",
      "subject": "docs(adr): accept ADR 0006 — parallel work without a pilot",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "docs/adr/0006-parallel-work-without-a-pilot.md"
      ]
    },
    "3ed807d0b006bf1be73c31cef350c9af53b0a10b": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-13T06:26:38Z",
      "body": "Design (F-9, F-10): the draft verb no longer reads gate frames out of\n`make verify` output. It sets ADR_ANSWERS_TOLERATE_CHANGE=<change> for that\none run; scripts/check_adr_answers.py then reports exactly that change's\nmissing answer without failing, so the exit code decides. Another change's\nmissing answer, a refused answer file and every other gate still fail, and\nno text a gate prints can matter. gate_sections, red_gates and\nonly_answer_owed are removed; answer_is_owed (examine) only decides the\n\"answer owed\" note after a green run. implement and repair are unchanged.\nF-11: only ADR files that exist now count as new (a deleted own ADR stays a\nkeep). F-12: quote_block never cuts the put-back path lines.\n\nRed first (baseline HEAD code + new tests, pytest exit 1 each):\ntest_a_verification_that_ended_right_after_the_adr_gate_owes_nothing,\ntest_a_failing_gate_printing_gate_frames_cannot_hide_its_red_frame,\ntest_a_rename_of_the_drafts_own_unmerged_adr_counts_one_adr,\ntest_put_back_paths_are_named_in_full_however_long. The criterion 13 test\nwas rewritten for the new mechanism (Broke a test: yes for F-9, F-10).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019EPak4XgNE5A3cvTW7eZ4G\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-10-07T06:52:32Z",
      "body": "A rule whose name starts with `secret:` is not applied to a file under the\nrepository's top-level tests/ folder: the working file, and the hunks of a\ncommit patch or of the staged diff that name such a file. Every other rule\nscans tests/ as before, and a secret rule scans everything outside it\n(tests_extra/, docs/tests/, a change's own folder, a link under tests/, a\ncommit message, a prompt text). A diff header that cannot be read with\ncertainty (a quoted name) is scanned in full.\n\nMaintainer's decision of 2026-10-07 on open item O-4 of the stage-2 change;\nthe accepted consequence is that a real key committed in a test file is not\nfound. The secret patterns live in the maintainer's denylist, not in this\nscript, so the marker is a name prefix and each machine sets it itself.\n\nThe log now runs with --no-renames (the staged scan already did) so a diff\nheader names one path, and splits message from patch by a marker line the log\nformat writes. Docstring and WORKFLOW state the exemption.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "decisions/gates.yaml",
        "provenance.yaml",
        "scripts/ci_gates.py"
      ]
    },

It stood without a class while docs/governance/regelwerk.md beside it is\nhuman-decided; the commit guard of the review-swarm runner could only refuse it\nthrough a hard-coded list (R-22 of the review-swarm review).\n\nThe maintainer's answer in the night interview of 2026-10-20 (Q-1, option A): the\nsame class as the rulebook. Gate changes then always travel as a decision pull\nrequest.\n",

    "bfc7cad6c84f758b0bee914199912eff602ca6f2": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T11:10:00Z",
      "body": "A second finding on the guard's binding tracking (after F6-4 and F6-5)\nends case repair. The guard now enumerates every way Python binds a\nname - plain and multiple-target assignment, tuple and list unpacking\npaired element-wise, starred, annotated and augmented assignment, the\nwalrus (bound in the enclosing function), for and comprehension targets,\nwith-as, parameter defaults, imports, definitions, except-as, match\ncaptures and del - and repeats until no new log binding appears. Every\nsuch binding shadows an enclosing one; comprehensions are scopes.\n\nA pathlib read_text, read_bytes, write_text or write_bytes is judged by\nits receiver only; its first argument counts only when called on a path\nclass or as a bare function. write_text's content is no destination.\n\nRed-first samples BINDING_FORMS, BINDING_SHADOWS and\nRECEIVER_DESTINATION; the spec's Boundary names what static analysis\ncannot follow (attributes, calls, unpairable containers, order).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "bfc7cad6c84f758b0bee914199912eff602ca6f2",
      "subject": "fix(flaky-swarm-leak-test): the guard follows every binding form (F6-6, F6-7)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "plans/changes/flaky-swarm-leak-test/spec.md"
      ]
    },

      "author_utc": "2026-11-13T23:38:23Z",
      "body": "The shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py) behind\nscripts/verify_all.sh and Stage 2: every unprotected (seconds) gate runs\nbefore admission and all red ones are reported together; only protected\ngates (cost minutes, or needs_admission) run under one admission; an\nunchanged tree reuses the cheap results, a changed one reruns them.\n\nOrchestrator hand implementation after three rejected runner attempts (two\npost-run checks red, the third model call ended with exit 1), approved by\nthe maintainer on 2026-11-13. Built on the tree of implement attempt 3\n(refs/stage2/attempts/verify-cheap-before-admission/implement-attempt-3-\n20261113T221950681498Z), with these repairs:\n\n- verify_run: no empty not-run header when the last gate was the stop.\n- verify_all.sh: keeps the duration_admission_context boundary, so an\n  ancestor's admission context is dropped and a nested run records reuse;\n  the attempt had removed it and its test block, both restored unchanged.\n- test fixtures: markers outside the measured tree, the release marker of\n  the nested proof reset, fake_git accepts the checkout argument.\n\nExisting tests changed because the spec changes the behaviour they pin:\n- tests/test_ci.py timing test (A): the start record is written before any\n  admission, so its admission_reused is unknown (None); the completion\n  record carries admission_requested False and no context. (B): the stop\n  at the first blocking gate is now proved among minutes gates, since the\n  cheap phase runs through every seconds gate (decisions Q-3).\n- the attempt's other changes to tests/test_ci.py, test_verify_cheap_first,\n  test_gate_catalog and test_stage2 (cost classes in fixtures, a git HEAD\n  for the tree measurement, the admission column, no whole-run admission\n  for the seconds-only document subset) follow the same spec criteria 2,\n  3, 5 and 10.\n\nChecked: ruff check and format clean over scripts/ and tests/; the new and\ndirectly touched test files 105 passed; tests/test_ci.py 179 passed,\n2 skipped.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

          "excerpt": "def validate_research_free_policy(policy: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Validate the entire selection policy before reading network sources.\"\"\"\n    keys = {\"provider\", \"suffix\", \"include\", \"exclude\"}\n    if not isinstance(policy, dict) or set(policy) != keys:\n        raise ResearchCatalogError(\"invalid free selection policy keys\", 2)\n    if policy[\"provider\"] != \"opencode-go\" or policy[\"suffix\"] != \"-free\":\n        raise ResearchCatalogError(\"invalid free provider or suffix\", 2)\n    for key in (\"include\", \"exclude\"):\n        values = policy[key]\n        if (\n            not isinstance(values, list)\n            or any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item.endswith(\"-free\") or item == \"-free\" for item in values)\n            or len(set(values)) != len(values)\n        ):\n            raise ResearchCatalogError(f\"invalid free selection {key}\", 2)\n",

          "excerpt": "def explore(\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    stage2_off: str | None = None,\n    klass: str | None = None,\n    availability_reported: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 1: the swarm for a feature or architectural change, GLM Flash for a bounded\n    change or a spike, or the explicit Haiku fallback - the answer lands in research.md.\"\"\"\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        klass = declared_class(root, change, klass)\n        if klass in SWARM_CLASSES:\n            import stage2_availability\n            import stage2_swarm\n\n            # The reported receipt comes first: no research call, probe or catalog read starts without it.\n            selection = stage2_availability.consume_research(\n                root, change, availability_reported, sys.modules[__name__], klass\n            )\n            stage2_swarm.run(root, change, sys.modules[__name__], klass, selection=selection)\n            return\n        if availability_reported is not None:\n            raise Refused(f\"--availability-reported belongs to a swarm class; this change is {klass}.\")\n        endpoint = GLM_FLASH\n    else:\n        if availability_reported is not None or klass is not None:\n            raise Refused(\"--stage2-off explores without a class or a selection receipt.\")\n        # The explicit Stage-1 route skips the class entirely: Haiku explores,\n        # and only the reason is carried for the later plan (spec, criterion 20).\n        endpoint = HAIKU\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, endpoint, bead_file=\"research.md\")\n    key = None\n    route = \"stage-1\" if stage2_off is not None else \"flash\"\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n    extra = (\n        f\"{EXPLORER_ROLE} \"\n        \"Report repository facts with source paths as prose ready to append to `research.md`. \"\n        \"Do not design, recommend, edit a file or use review-table formatting.\"\n    )\n    prompt = work_prompt(root, \"01-explore.md\", change, extra)\n    begin_work_call(ctx, \"explore\", endpoint, prompt, 1, route, ctx.research, stage2_off)\n    answer = run_work_model(ctx, prompt, endpoint, writable=False, key=key)\n    if not names_a_repository_file(root, answer):\n        # Research names its sources; an answer that names no file of the repository is a refusal or a\n        # question, not research, and is shown rather than appended (bead coding-harness-e7m).\n        tail = \"\\n\".join(answer.strip().splitlines()[-40:])\n        print(f\"explore: the answer, as it came:\\n{tail}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        raise CallFailed(\"the exploration answer names no file of the repository; nothing was appended\")\n    # The publication, not a plain append: the header's provenance fields are corrected and the skeleton's\n    # opening notices removed in the same atomic replacement that lands the answer (spec, criteria 1-5).\n    prepared = research_publication(\n        ctx.research.read_bytes(), producer=producer_for(endpoint), day=today(), model=endpoint[1]\n    )\n    publis",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::launch",
          "end_line": 1129,
          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)\n        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        what = limit or f\"the reviewer time limit after {REVIEWER_MINUTES:",

      "statement": "Every attempt-level helper a new attempt module would reuse is parameterised by `root: Path` and acts inside it (`worktree_tree`, `attempt_files`, `attempt_has_work`, `restore_baseline`, `checkpoint`, `verify_attempt`, `refuse_preexisting`, `changed_paths`), and `launch` starts every foreign program with `cwd=root`; `run_codex` and `run_work_model` therefore take their working directory from `ctx.root`, which is also where the prompt builders read `AGENTS.md`, `prompts/*` and the change folder.           "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. This records only the\n    runner's own deletions. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check ",

      "statement": "`tool_state`/`tool_problem` already handle a symlinked `.venv` root, which is the shape Q-3's link produces: the root link target is recorded (`.venv` -> `link:<target>`) and the tools behind the link are hashed, so an overwrite through the link is detected.           "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def _private_repository(root: Path, destination: Path, checkout: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create a proof's private repository at `destination`, its checkout materialized at `checkout`.\n\n    The clone carries the source's objects wholesale - unreferenced ones included - with no\n    hardlinks and no object alternates, so the proof runs against bytes of its own and a local\n    object copy carries the fixed tree `worktree_tree` wrote without a ref. Every source ref is\n    preserved under its own name first, so a ref the source already had stays a move in the\n    proof's store, not an accidental creation; the remote configuration goes, so an ordinary\n    Git operation in the proof has no path back to the source. HEAD is detached at `checkout`\n    when it names the baseline commit, or at the source's HEAD for a fixed-code tree id.\n    `checkout` is read into the index and the working tree, leaving a baseline clean against\n    its own commit. The source's refs, index and worktree are read here, never\n    written (spec, criteria 1 and 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Snapshot before copying objects: later source refs may name objects the clone never saw.\n    refs = _ref_targets(root)\n    head = refs.pop(\"HEAD\").split(\" \", 1)[0]\n    _git_output(root, \"clone\", \"--quiet\", \"--no-hardlinks\", str(root), str(destination))\n    # An alternates file makes the clone depend on another object store. Git\n    # otherwise refuses both names in one transaction, even with --no-deref.\n    _git_output(\n        destination,\n        \"update-ref\",\n        \"--no-deref\",\n        \"--stdin\",\n        stdin=(\n            f\"start\\nupdate HEAD {head}\\nprepare\\ncommit\\nstart\\n\"\n            + \"\".join(f\"update {name} {target}\\n\" for name, target in refs.items() if \" \" not in target)\n            + \"prepare\\ncommit\\n\"\n        ),\n    )\n    # Measurements retain both the resolved object and symbolic target. Restore\n    # symbolic refs by kind, using symbolic-ref for Git versions without symref-update.\n    for name, target in refs.items():\n        _, _, symbolic = target.partition(\" \")\n        if symbolic:\n            _git_output(destination, \"symbolic-ref\", name, symbolic)\n    _git_output(destination, \"read-tree\", \"--reset\", \"-u\", checkout)\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

without it, only report\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--budget-seconds\", type=float, help=\"startup budget shared by closures and publication\")\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n    if args.budget_seconds is not None and args.budget_seconds <= 0:\n        ap.error(\"--budget-seconds must be positive\")\n    deadline = time.monotonic() + args.budget_seconds if args.budget_seconds is not None else None\n\n    if args.write and os.environ.get(bead_render.UMGEBUNGS_RENDER, \"\").strip():\n        print(\n            f\"close-merged: refusing to write with {bead_render.UMGEBUNGS_RENDER} set — the state would be a \"\n            \"preset render, not this machine's tracker;           "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_tree(root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The tree id of the worktree as git counts it, written through a temporary index.\n\n    Seed a fresh index with the real index's path, mode and object entries, including newly\n    force-added ignored files, never inheriting flags that could hide changes. Then add current\n    contents without forcing ignored, untracked children of a replaced path into the tree.\n    The real index is only read; it, the stash and the refs are never\n    changed (spec, criterion 10).\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        temporary_index = Path(tmp) / \"index\"\n        tracked = _git_bytes(root, \"ls-files\", \"-s\", \"-z\")\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(temporary_index)}\n        _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", \"--empty\", env=env)\n        if tracked:\n            _git_bytes(\n                root,\n                \"update-index\",\n                \"-z\",\n                \"--index-info\",\n                env=env,\n                stdin=tracked,\n            )\n        _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", env=env)\n        return _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). The one list, with a reason per\n   tool, is `scripts/omnigent_policy.py`. Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list. It refuses the denied ones and asks about the asked one\n   server-side for every Omnigent session on the machine. The\n   maintainer installs it, and nothing here depends on it alone (ADR 0006); as of\n   2026-09-29 it is built but not installed. Omnigent's bridge runs its own\n   `sys_os_*` tools without any policy while its relay does not advertise them,\n   and there only the rule in `.claude/settings.json` holds. Not yet measured: whether `omnigent claude`\n   started inside a worktree keeps that directory as the session's working\n   directory in every case.\n6. **After the merge, the worktree goes.** `git worktree remove\n   .claude/worktrees/<name>` and the branch with it. A worktree nobody works in\n   is a place where a later session finds an old state and takes it for the\n   current one.\n\nIsolation between sessions is a working agreement, not a wall: worktrees share\ngit's refs, hooks and configuration (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-gap-analysis.md`).\nWhat really does not happen is simultaneous writing *to the same change* — that\nis not a tool question but a division of work.\n\n**What i",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::worktree_digests",
          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_model_call_saves_the_attempt_before_restoring(\n    world: World, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    # Bead coding-harness-znc. Planted fault: the restore runs without the snapshot, and an\n    # attempt's edits - hours of them when a budget runs out - are gone with it.\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"budget spent\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    err = capsys.readouterr().err\n    refs = git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname)\", \"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/\").splitlines()\n    assert len(refs) == 1 and refs[0].startswith(\"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/implement-attempt-1-\")\n    assert refs[0] in err and \"restored the worktree\" in err\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", f\"{refs[0]}^\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/half.py\") == \"x = 1\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/app.py\").endswith(\"# edit\")\n    # The snapshot carries the runner's identity, not the machine's: CI has no git user (PR #153).\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>\", refs[0]) == (\n        \"stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>|stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>\"\n    )\n    # The restore still leaves the tree clean and HEAD and the real index untouched.\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n",

          "end_line": 11036,
          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2).           "excerpt": "def preflight(\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    bead_file: str = \"spec.md\",\n    required: tuple[str, ...] = (),\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n) -> Context:\n    \"\"\"The refusals that precede everything else: change, artefacts and declaration.\n\n    `admission_problem` replaces the individual declaration for the free class:\n    it receives the root and the model id and returns a problem or None (ADR\n    0021, decision 3). Every other call keeps the strict declaration.\n    \"\"\"\n    folder = folder_of(root, change)\n    bead = _artefact_bead(folder / bead_file)\n    if bead is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"plans/changes/{change}/{bead_file} has no bead in its header; the runner cannot name the work.\")\n    for name in required:\n        path = folder / name\n        try:\n            path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"plans/changes/{change}/{name} cannot be read.\") from error\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return Context(root, change, folder, bead, go_admission=admission_problem)\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=__doc__,\n        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n        allow_abbrev=False,\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"verb\", choices=sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"]))\n    parser.add_argument(\"change\", nargs=\"?\", default=\"\", help=\"folder name under plans/changes/\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"row_status\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ROW=STATUS\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the loop row and its new status, e.g. 'L1-1=taken — not a test'; \"\n            \"refuses ordinary taken for test-only locations: use taken — not a test — <reason>\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"reason_text\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the decision's own single-line reason; \"\n            \"the Broke a test proof mark stays the runner's; triage supplies no repair evidence\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage2-off\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        const=\"stage 2 disabled by caller\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=\"use the Stage-1 route for explore, implement or repair and record the optional reason\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--model\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: the model id, exactly as model-endpoints.yaml lists it\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--class\",\n        dest=\"klass\",\n        default=None,\n        choices=CLASSES,\n        help=\"explore only: the change class before a spec exists, agreeing with every stated one\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        dest=\"availability_reported\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ID\",\n        help=(\n            \"the id printed by prepare-loop (review-loop) or prepare-explore (explore, swarm classes) \"\n            \"after its selection was reported to the maintainer\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--seats\",\n        action=\"append\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TRIO=MODELS\",\n        help=\"prepare-explore only: the maintainer's Go models for a trio, e.g. repository=a,b\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--handover\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: a handover file inside the worktree (default: the change's handover.md)\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"MODEL\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: retire the stage this model belongs to, so the loop can go on\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--reason\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TEXT\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: why the stage is retired or the loop restarted; repeat for every active other-worktree key a refusal names\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"--root\", default=str(REPO_ROOT), help=argparse.SUPPRESS)\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    _LAUNCH_STOPPED.clear()\n    # SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT stop the run like Ctrl-C: the running programs' groups are\n    # killed before the exit (DL-B-5, F6-8).           "excerpt": "def test_targeted_mode_is_repair_only(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 10 (repair-targeted-check). Planted fault: a verb takes the targeted route without naming\n    it at its call site, or the draft's document check returns to the admitted shell runner.\"\"\"\n    for function in (stage2.run_attempts, stage2.verify_attempt):\n        name = \"verify_mode\" if function is stage2.run_attempts else \"mode\"\n        assert inspect.signature(function).parameters[name].default == \"full\"\n    # Exactly the two work verbs name the targeted mode at their call sites; every other caller keeps\n    # the admitted full check as its default (bead coding-harness-0swp).\n    source = (REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"stage2.py\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert \"REPAIR_VERIFY_MODE\" not in source\n    assert source.count('verify_mode=\"targeted\"') == 2\n    # A covered implement runs the targeted check, never the document-only draft subset:\n    commands = targeted_mode(monkeypatch)\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"implemented\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 2\\n\", \"tests/test_fix.py\": FIX_TEST},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            }\n        ],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 0\n    assert commands.of(\"pytest\") and commands.of(\"gate\"), \"the targeted route did not run\"\n    assert commands.of(\"make\") == [], \"a covered implement ran the admitted full check\"\n    # The draft's document check stays out of the admitted shell runner:\n    ctx = stage2.Context(world.root, \"demo\", world.plan.parent, \"demo-1\")\n    world.plan.write_text(PLAN_CARD, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    _problems, _owed, scope = stage2.verify_draft(world.root, ctx, None, [], stage2.tool_state(world.root))\n    assert world.calls(\"bash\") == [], \"the draft's document check went through bash again\"\n    assert commands.of(\"make\") == []\n    assert \"document checks only\" in scope and \"result: green\" in scope\n",

          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "record_key",
          "start_line": 4053,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::worktree_digests",
          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "worktree_digests",
          "start_line": 3482,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/machine_facts.py::worktree_field",
          "end_line": 203,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/machine_facts.py",
          "reference": "worktree_field",
          "start_line": 193,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "tests/test_machine_facts.py::test_worktrees_count_registered_non_bare_entries",
          "end_line": 263,
          "excerpt": "def test_worktrees_count_registered_non_bare_entries(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: the main checkout, a linked or stale registration, a bare entry or a path with\n    whitespace yields the wrong count, or an unrelated filesystem directory is counted\n    (spec criterion 4).\"\"\"\n    worktree = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    (worktree / \"unrelated\").mkdir(parents=True)  # a real directory git has never registered\n    outputs = {\n        **git_keys(worktree),\n        (\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"): worktree_list_fixture(\n            MAIN, LINKED, STALE, BARE\n        ),\n    }\n    run = fake_run(outputs)\n    out = machine_facts.render(\n        snapshot(run, fake_statvfs({worktree: statvfs_result(GIB)}), cwd=worktree, proc_dir=proc_fixture(tmp_path))\n    )\n    line = next(line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith(\"registered worktrees:\"))\n    assert line == \"registered worktrees: 3 (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n    assert \"/repo/bare\" not in out and \"linked wt\" not in out  # paths never print; entries are counted only\n    assert \"unrelated\" not in out  # the count comes from git's table, never the directory listing\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_machine_facts.py",
          "reference": "test_worktrees_count_registered_non_bare_entries",
          "start_line": 244,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "Registered worktrees are a public enumeration of this repository: record_key(change, root) hashes the resolved root, worktree_digests reads `git worktree list --porcelain` and turns every listed path into that digest, and machine_facts.worktree_field counts every non-bare entry with \"stale registrations included\" — so an attempt worktree that git registers under the temporary directory would enter both the runner's record-key set and the run report's worktree count."

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Planted fault: the restore runs without the snapshot, and an\n    # attempt's edits - hours of them when a budget runs out - are gone with it.\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"budget spent\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    err = capsys.readouterr().err\n    refs = git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname)\", \"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/\").splitlines()\n    assert len(refs) == 1 and refs[0].startswith(\"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/implement-attempt-1-\")\n    assert refs[0] in err and \"restored the worktree\" in err\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", f\"{refs[0]}^\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/half.py\") == \"x = 1\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/app.py\").endswith(\"# edit\")\n    # The snapshot carries the runner's identity, not the machine's: CI has no git user (PR #153).\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>\", refs[0]) == (\n        \"stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>|stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>\"\n    )\n    # The restore still leaves the tree clean and HEAD and the real index untouched.\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::tool_state",
          "end_line": 5630,
          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    ",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names.
